quote: Furthermore, agonists of stimulatory checkpoint pathways such as OX40, ICOS, GITR, 4-1BB, CD40, or molecules targeting tumor microenvironment components like IDO or TLR are under investigation.
summary: Cancer checkpoint review that lists ICOS agonists among stimulatory pathways under investigation; nothing specific about ICOS or colitis.

quote: In the lungs of nonsensitized naive mice, IL-33-responsive cells were identified that have a lymphoid morphology, lack lineage markers, highly express CD25, CD44, Thy1.2, ICOS, Sca-1, and IL-7Rα (i.e., Lin(-)CD25(+)CD44(hi) lymphoid cells), and require IL-7Rα for their development.
summary: ICOS is only one of several surface markers of IL-33-responsive lung lymphoid cells in allergic airway mice; no ICOS-specific result.

quote: In mice, butyrate restrains anti-CTLA-4-induced up-regulation of CD80/CD86 on dendritic cells and ICOS on T cells, accumulation of tumor-specific T cells and memory T cells.
summary: In cancer models, butyrate dampens anti-CTLA-4-induced ICOS up-regulation on T cells; ICOS is one of several readouts and no colitis data are given.

quote: Each of those elements is essential, because loss of c-Maf, IL-21-signaling, or ICOS decreases the frequency of IL-27-induced differentiation of IL-10-producing Tr1 cells.
summary: Loss of ICOS reduces IL-27-driven differentiation of IL-10-producing Tr1 cells in mouse T cells; no colitis or barrier outcome was measured.

quote: Unexpectedly, ILC2-intrinsic IL-33 activation was required for Treg cell accumulation in vivo and was independent of ILC2 type 2 cytokines but partially dependent on direct co-stimulatory interactions via ICOSL-ICOS.
summary: ICOSL-ICOS interaction is mentioned as partly contributing to ILC2-driven Treg accumulation in adipose tissue; ICOS itself is not the focus.

quote: Antibodies to watch in 2020.
summary: Annual antibody pipeline overview that only notes a Phase 3 anti-ICOS antibody in head and neck cancer; nothing about UC.

quote: In contrast, CD44(hi)CD62L(lo)CCR7(lo) T reg cells that populate nonlymphoid tissues do not access IL-2-prevalent regions in vivo and are insensitive to IL-2 blockade; instead, their maintenance depends on continued signaling through the co-stimulatory receptor ICOS (inducible co-stimulator).
summary: Maintenance of tissue-resident regulatory T cells in mice depends on ICOS signalling; no colitis or inflammation outcome was measured.

quote: Blockade of ICOS rapidly converts early insulitis to diabetes, which disrupts the balance of Teffs and Tregs and promotes a very broad shift in the expression of the T regulatory-specific profile.
summary: Blocking ICOS in prediabetic mice rapidly turns insulitis into diabetes by disrupting Treg control, showing ICOS-dependent Tregs restrain autoimmune inflammation.

quote: Mechanistically, the costimulatory molecule ICOS activated mTORC1 and mTORC2 to drive glycolysis and lipogenesis, and glucose transporter 1-mediated glucose metabolism promoted Tfh cell responses.
summary: ICOS is described as an upstream activator of mTOR signalling in Tfh cells; the paper's perturbations target mTOR, not ICOS, and no colitis data.

quote: Liver (vs. lung) irradiation produced greater T-cell activation, reflected as increases in the proportions of peripheral T cells expressing ICOS, GITR, and 4-1BB.
summary: In a cancer radiotherapy plus ipilimumab trial, ICOS is one of several T-cell activation markers raised after liver irradiation; not tested as a predictor.

quote: The group 2 innate lymphoid cell (ILC2) regulatory network and its underlying mechanisms.
summary: Review of ILC2 regulation that lists ICOSL-ICOS as one cell-to-cell interaction; no specific data or UC relevance for ICOS.

quote: The frequency of circulating OX40L-expressing myeloid APCs positively correlated with disease activity and the frequency of ICOS(+) blood Tfh cells in SLE.
summary: ICOS is only used as a Tfh cell marker in a lupus study of OX40L; no gene-specific result relevant to UC.

quote: Anti-CTLA-4 therapy results in higher CD4+ICOShi T cell frequency and IFN-gamma levels in both nonmalignant and malignant prostate tissues.
summary: CD4+ICOShi T cells are proposed as an immunologic marker to monitor patients on anti-CTLA-4 therapy in bladder and prostate cancer.

quote: Combination therapy was associated with sustained peripheral elevations in: Th1-type cytokines, activated (ICOS+) and proliferating (Ki67+) CD4+ and CD8+ T cells, and posttreatment proliferative T-effector cells relative to T-regulatory cells within tumor.
summary: ICOS+ T cells are one of several immune activation readouts after ipilimumab in breast cancer patients; no gene-specific analysis.

quote: ST2(+) Treg represent an activated subset of Foxp3(+) cells, demonstrated to be ICOS(high)CD44(high) compared with their ST2(-) counterparts.
summary: ICOS is used as a phenotype marker of IL-33-responsive ST2+ Tregs; the paper does not test ICOS function.

quote: Positive regulation of ILC-2s through ICOS has been recently elucidated.
summary: ICOS is only mentioned as prior background on ILC2 regulation in a paper focused on PD-1.

quote: CD8(+) Tregs express more activation or proliferation markers such as CTLA-4, ICOS, and Ki-67 than other CD8(+) T cells.
summary: ICOS appears among activation markers higher on CD8+ regulatory T cells; no ICOS-specific experiment or colitis data.

quote: Using cell-based artificial APCs we found that CD28 but not ICOS, OX40, 4-1BB, CD27, or CD40 ligand costimulation maintained high levels of Foxp3 expression and in vitro suppressive function.
summary: ICOS costimulation did not maintain human Treg Foxp3 expression or suppressive function in vitro, unlike CD28; no colitis outcome.

quote: ICOS<sup>+</sup> Tregs: A Functional Subset of Tregs in Immune Diseases.
summary: Review of ICOS+ Tregs in autoimmune, allergic and cancer settings, noting ICOS as a potential biomarker and antibody target; no new data.

quote: These data suggest that the B7h-ICOS costimulatory pathway may be important in IEC:T-cell interactions.
summary: B7h Ig, the ICOS ligand, inhibited proliferation of IEC-stimulated T cells in coculture, and IBD epithelial cells expressed B7h; the pathway's effect on inflammation is unclear.

quote: The corolla captured engaged CD28, ICOS, CD226 and SLAM-F1 co-stimulators.
summary: ICOS is one of several co-stimulators captured in the CD2 corolla at the immunological synapse; no ICOS-specific finding.

quote: Higher numbers of activated ICOS+ conventional CD4+ T cells were observed in αCTLA-4-induced colitis compared with patients with IBD.
summary: ICOS+ conventional CD4+ T cells are more abundant in anti-CTLA-4-induced colitis than in IBD, where ICOS+ cells are mainly Tregs.

quote: IDO is regulated by IFN-γ and other cytokines and by nitric oxide.
summary: Review of kynurenine pathway regulation in which IDO is the rate-limiting enzyme outside the liver; no UC-specific data.

quote: Therefore, strategies to block IDO might enhance the effectiveness of tumor immunotherapy.
summary: Review of IDO as a mediator of tumour-induced immune tolerance and a cancer immunotherapy target; no colitis data.

quote: Furthermore, agonists of stimulatory checkpoint pathways such as OX40, ICOS, GITR, 4-1BB, CD40, or molecules targeting tumor microenvironment components like IDO or TLR are under investigation.
summary: Cancer checkpoint review that mentions IDO only in passing among targets under investigation.
